attrs.label: SaaS content has to sell the product
attrs.html:
SaaS content has to sell the product

Traffic is easy to buy. Sign-ups from content are what matter. Pick a challenge to see how we handle it.

The challengeLarger competitors publish every day and already own the obvious topics. Writing the same posts later rarely wins.

Our approach

Win the searches they ignore, closest to your product and to a sign-up.

You don’t beat a 20-person content team by publishing more. You beat them by being more useful on the searches closest to a buying decision, where they’re often thin.

In practice

  • A review of the searches your competitors rank for, and the ones they don’t
  • Comparison, use-case and integration pages before broad blog posts
  • Detailed guides that need real product knowledge to write
  • Regular checks for competitor pages that have gone out of date

Why it matters

Small teams win in search by picking their battles. The right 30 pages beat 300 generic ones.

Methods we use

  1. 1Search gap review

    Topics your buyers search for that big competitors cover badly or not at all.

  2. 2Bottom-of-funnel first

    Comparison, use-case and integration pages before broad blog posts.

  3. 3Niche depth

    The detailed guides only a team that knows the product can write.

  4. 4Faster refreshes

    We update pages quickly when competitors’ content goes stale.

What you get

  • A search gap map
  • A prioritised content plan
  • Quick-win pages

The challengeGeneric productivity posts bring in readers who have no reason to try your product.

Our approach

Show your product doing the job the reader came for.

Readers don’t sign up because of a blog post. They sign up because a post showed them how your product solves their problem. So the product belongs in the content.

In practice

  • Writers get an account and use the product before writing
  • Real screenshots and workflows in every guide
  • Free templates that open straight in your product
  • A call to action that fits what the reader just learned

Why it matters

Product-led content turns readers into trials. Generic content turns readers into readers.

Methods we use

  1. 1Hands-on product time

    Our writers use your product before they write about it.

  2. 2Real screenshots and steps

    Workflows shown in the product, not stock images.

  3. 3Templates that open in the app

    Free templates readers can use straight away in your product.

  4. 4Natural calls to action

    A reason to sign up that fits each piece, not a banner at the end.

What you get

  • Product-led guides
  • Free templates
  • In-post calls to action

The challengeEvery release makes screenshots, steps and feature pages a little more out of date.

Our approach

Keep content as current as the product, with a kit for every release.

SaaS products change every few weeks. Without a plan, your best content slowly starts showing screens and steps that no longer exist.

In practice

  • A launch kit for every major release
  • A map of which pages show which product screens
  • A quarterly check of top pages against the current product
  • Release notes customers actually want to read

Why it matters

Out-of-date screenshots make buyers wonder what else is out of date.

Methods we use

  1. 1Release launch kits

    A feature page update, launch article, help guide, email and posts for each release.

  2. 2Screenshot tracking

    A list of which pages show which screens, so updates take hours, not weeks.

  3. 3Quarterly refreshes

    Older pieces checked against the current product every quarter.

  4. 4Changelog content

    Release notes written for customers, not engineers.

What you get

  • Launch kits
  • A screenshot map
  • Quarterly refreshes

The challengePeople sign up, look around and never come back. Content often stops at the sign-up button.

Our approach

Help new users reach their first result in their first week.

A sign-up is only the start. If new users don’t reach a first result quickly, they don’t convert to paid. Content can guide them there.

In practice

  • We find the steps activated users take in their first days
  • Short guides for each of those steps
  • Trial emails that send the next guide at the right time
  • In-app copy that keeps people moving

Why it matters

Better activation means more paying customers from the same number of trials.

Methods we use

  1. 1Activation research

    We look at what activated users do in their first days.

  2. 2Onboarding guides

    Short guides that walk users to that first result.

  3. 3Trial email sequences

    Emails that send the right guide at the right moment.

  4. 4In-app help copy

    Empty states, tooltips and checklists written to keep users moving.

What you get

  • Onboarding guides
  • Trial emails
  • In-app copy

The challengeBuyers search “you vs them” and “alternatives to”, and competitors or review sites answer first.

Our approach

Be the honest answer when buyers compare you.

Buyers comparing tools are close to a decision. If your competitor or a review site answers their “you vs them” search, they shape the decision.

In practice

  • We use competitors’ products and note the real differences
  • Fair comparison pages that say who each tool suits
  • Alternatives pages for buyers leaving a competitor
  • Battle cards for sales, from the same research

Why it matters

Honest comparison pages win trust, and trust wins close decisions.

Methods we use

  1. 1Competitor research

    We sign up for competitors and note the real differences.

  2. 2Honest comparison pages

    Fair “you vs them” pages that say who each tool is best for.

  3. 3Alternatives pages

    Pages for buyers leaving a competitor, with migration steps.

  4. 4Sales battle cards

    The same research, turned into one-pagers for your sales team.

What you get

  • Comparison pages
  • Alternatives pages
  • Battle cards

The challengeYou connect to dozens of tools, but there’s one list page and nothing that ranks.

Our approach

Turn every integration into a page that brings in the right users.

People search for tools that work with the software they already use. Every integration you have is a search you could be ranking for.

In practice

  • A page for each integration, with set-up steps
  • Workflow recipes that combine your product with the other tool
  • Joint content with your integration partners
  • One template that keeps every page consistent

Why it matters

Integration searches bring in users who already have the problem and the tools to solve it.

Methods we use

  1. 1A page per integration

    What it does, who it’s for and how to set it up.

  2. 2Use-case recipes

    Step-by-step workflows that combine your product with the other tool.

  3. 3Partner co-marketing

    Guest posts and joint content with your integration partners.

  4. 4Templates at scale

    A page structure that keeps hundreds of pages consistent.

What you get

  • Integration pages
  • Workflow recipes
  • Partner content

The challengePage views look good in reports, but they don’t pay for the programme.

Our approach

Report in trials, activation and revenue, piece by piece.

If content is reported in page views, it gets judged on page views. We report what your board cares about: trials, activation and revenue.

In practice

  • Content visits connected to sign-ups in your product analytics
  • A list of which pieces new trials read first
  • A monthly report on trials, activation and paid conversions
  • Quarterly reviews of where to spend next

Why it matters

When you can show trials and revenue from content, the programme pays for itself on paper too.

Methods we use

  1. 1Product analytics set-up

    Content visits connected to sign-ups and activation in your analytics.

  2. 2Trials by piece

    Which pieces each new trial read before signing up.

  3. 3A monthly report

    Readers, trials, activation and paid conversions, in plain English.

  4. 4Quarterly reviews

    What to do more of, what to fix and what to stop.

What you get

  • Trial attribution
  • A monthly report
  • Quarterly reviews

SaaS content from first search to activation

Pick a stage to see what users need from you then, and the content we create for it.

Stage 1 of 4

Attract

What buyers are thinking

Get found by people with the problem you solve
How we measure it
Readers from search, template downloads, AI citations

3 content types for this stage

attrs.title: SaaS content marketing questions, answered
attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: What is SaaS content marketing?
items.answer: SaaS content marketing is creating content, such as guides, templates, comparison and integration pages, that attracts people with the problem your software solves and shows them how your product solves it.

items.question: What does a SaaS content marketing agency do?
items.answer: It learns your product, maps content to your features and buyers, writes and edits the content, keeps it up to date with releases and reports on trials and sign-ups.

items.question: What is product-led content?
items.answer: Content that teaches something useful and shows your product doing it, with real screenshots and workflows, so readers see why they’d want it.

items.question: How much does SaaS content marketing cost?
items.answer: Every programme is a fixed monthly price, based on your stage and how much content you need. We quote after a free 30-minute call.

items.question: How long until content brings in trials?
items.answer: Comparison pages and templates can bring in trials within two to three months. Wider programmes build over six to twelve months.

items.question: Do you use AI to write content?
items.answer: No. Every piece is written and edited by people who have used your product.
